---
title: "STAT 579: Final Paper Grading Rubric"
---

This rubric outlines the criteria for evaluating your final project paper. The paper is graded out of 100 points and accounts for 25% of your final course grade. Each component will be assessed on its clarity, rigor, and thoughtful application of causal inference principles.

| Component | Weight | Criteria for Excellence (A) | Criteria for Proficiency (B) | Criteria for Developing (C/Below) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Intro & Background** | 10 pts | Causal question is precise and well-motivated with relevant literature. A clear gap in knowledge is established. | Causal question is clear. Motivation is adequate but may lack depth or context. | Causal question is vague or associational. Motivation is unclear or missing. |
| **Methods: Target Trial Protocol** | 20 pts | All 7 components of the target trial are explicitly and precisely defined. The emulation strategy is well-justified and transparent about any deviations from the ideal. | Most components of the trial are defined. The link between the ideal trial and the emulation could be clearer. Some details are ambiguous. | The target trial is not specified or is missing major components. The emulation is poorly defined. |
| **Methods: Causal Assumptions & DAG** | 20 pts | Final DAG is well-justified. Exchangeability, positivity, and consistency are clearly stated and discussed in the context of the study. Potential violations are thoughtfully considered. | A DAG is present. Key assumptions are stated but the discussion of their plausibility is superficial or unclear. | DAG is missing or incorrect. No clear statement or understanding of the core causal assumptions. |
| **Methods: Statistical Analysis** | 15 pts | The chosen statistical method (e.g., IPW, g-comp) is appropriate and correctly implemented. Details (e.g., PS model specification, diagnostics) are clear and well-documented. | The method is appropriate, but implementation details are sparse or diagnostics are incomplete. | The chosen statistical method is inappropriate for the question, or its implementation is incorrect. |
| **Results** | 15 pts | Results are presented clearly and logically (e.g., Table 1, balance plots, effect estimates). Figures are well-labeled and easy to interpret. A relevant sensitivity analysis (e.g., E-value) is performed and reported correctly. | Key results are present but may be poorly organized or labeled. The sensitivity analysis is missing or misinterpreted. | Results are missing, incorrect, or presented in a confusing way. No attempt at sensitivity analysis. |
| **Discussion & Conclusion** | 15 pts | Thoughtful interpretation of findings. Limitations are discussed with a deep focus on the key causal assumptions. Connects results back to the scientific literature and discusses implications. | Interpretation is plausible but superficial. Limitations are listed without a deep connection to the study's causal validity. | Results are misinterpreted. Discussion of limitations is absent or irrelevant. |
| **Overall Quality** | 5 pts | The paper is exceptionally well-written, professionally formatted, and easy to follow. The R code appendix is clean and reproducible. | The paper is generally well-written but may have minor errors in formatting, grammar, or clarity. | The paper is difficult to read due to major issues with writing, structure, or formatting. |
